correctness.rationale: Minuscule weight theory gives a single Weyl orbit of weights with multiplicity one. A generic integral cocharacter separates this finite weight set, so the ambient projective fixed locus is exactly the set of weight lines. Every weight line is a Weyl translate of the highest-weight line and therefore lies on the closed homogeneous orbit. Each secant variety is torus-stable and contains the closed orbit, hence its fixed locus equals the full ambient fixed locus. Euler localization for algebraic \(\mathbb C^*\)-actions, valid for singular varieties by Rosenlicht stratification, gives the Euler characteristic as the number of weights, namely \(\dim V_\lambda\). Constructible additivity then gives zero compactly supported Euler characteristic for every higher exact secant layer. The package checker independently replays weight separation in type A, half-spin, and even-quadric classical models.

value.rationale: Minuscule homogeneous varieties are foundational projective varieties, and their secant towers encode border-rank geometry for skew tensors, spinors, and exceptional representations. Secant dimensions, equations, singularities, and orbit structures change substantially with rank, yet the theorem shows that ordinary Euler characteristic is completely frozen throughout every such tower. The exact-layer vanishing gives a uniform topological constraint on all higher secant-rank strata and explains several family-specific fixed-point phenomena through one representation-theoretic mechanism. This is a structural all-family theorem, not a routine parameter increment.
